subject: Materials Science
title: Galvanic Corrosion: Mixed Metal Trouble
description: A quick win: understand Galvanic Corrosion: Mixed Metal Trouble.

hook.text: The Statue of Liberty's copper skin and iron framework created a giant galvanic cell — it corroded for a century.

buildup.text: When two dissimilar metals contact in an electrolyte, the more active metal corrodes preferentially.

discovery.text: A small anode connected to a large cathode corrodes devastatingly fast — area ratio matters enormously.

twist.text: Steel bolts in an aluminum structure will corrode the aluminum — even though steel is stronger.

climax.text: The 1984 Statue of Liberty restoration replaced the iron framework with stainless steel to stop galvanic attack.

punchline.text: Mix the wrong metals and one volunteers to dissolve for the other.

quiz.question: What makes galvanic corrosion worse?
options: A small anode area relative to a large cathode area
Using metals close together on the galvanic series
